claims.text: As-deposited nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi films possess interfacial strain.
As-deposited sputtered FeMnNiGeSi films have characteristic defect distributions.
A 2–3 nm Al2O3 overlayer can be deposited immediately after film deposition by ALD below 100°C.
Keeping the ALD temperature below 100°C will preserve the native FeMnNiGeSi nanostructure.
The Al2O3 overlayer will reduce substrate-induced interfacial strain.
Reducing interfacial strain will mitigate magnetoelastic pinning in FeMnNiGeSi films.
Interfacial-strain changes can be quantified using X-ray diffraction and TEM strain mapping.
A dielectric overlayer on the exposed film surface will decouple the film from both the substrate and environmental fluctuations.
Surface decoupling will reduce local strain-induced magnetic pinning centers.
Reduced pinning will promote more reversible domain-wall motion during magnetic-cooling cycles.
More reversible domain-wall motion will sharpen the magnetocaloric response.
Coated films will have lower coercivity than uncoated as-deposited films.
Coated films will have narrower magnetic hysteresis loops than uncoated films.
Coated films will exhibit an enhanced and sharper low-field magnetocaloric peak.
Improvements in coercivity, hysteresis, and magnetocaloric response will correlate with measured reductions in interfacial strain.
The uncoated baseline has significant strain-induced domain-wall pinning that causes notable hysteresis and a less pronounced magnetocaloric response.
The predicted coating benefits apply at fields below approximately 50–100 Oe.
Magnetic-cooling cycle frequency is limited by heat-transfer rate.
Fields above the stated low-field range may eliminate the coating's predicted benefits.
Thermally changing the film nanostructure may eliminate the coating's predicted benefits.

contradictions.description: The intervention places Al2O3 on top of the already-deposited film, whereas the mechanism says this surface overlayer decouples the film from its substrate. The proposed geometry does not insert a decoupling layer at the film–substrate interface.
